terms.comment: The grammarians’ Greek word, ‘the rule and method of writing’ (Suet. Aug. 88.1), which Quintilian renders rēctē scrībendī scientia (1.7.1); Lewis & Short: post-Augustan. To spell is simply scrībere: rēctē scrībere, to spell correctly (Traupman 29, 248). Morgan–Owens: I’m terrible at spelling, orthographiam haudquāquam calleō. To spell a word with a letter is scrībere per with the accusative (Quint. 1.7.5; Traupman 248).

terms.gloss: the way a word is written, spelling
evidence: Caecin. ap. Cic. Fam. 6.7.1: mendum scrīptūrae, a slip in writing (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Writing in general, and the written form of a word.

phrases.latin: Orthographiam, id est fōrmulam ratiōnemque scrībendī ā grammaticīs īnstitūtam, nōn adeō custōdiit
phrases.english: He did not keep closely to spelling, that is, the rule and method of writing laid down by the grammarians

phrases.latin: quod Graecī ὀρθογραφίαν vocant; hoc nōs rēctē scrībendī scientiam nōminēmus
phrases.english: what the Greeks call orthography; let us call it the science of writing correctly
How do you spell this word?

phrases.latin: itemque cum, sī tempus significāret, per qu, sī comitem, per c ac duās sequentēs scrīberētur
phrases.english: and that cum should be spelt with qu if it meant time, with c and the two following letters if it meant company

phrases.latin: Quīdam scrībunt «cum» per «q» litteram, sī tempus significat.
phrases.english: Some spell “cum” with a “q” if it means time.
